title.title: Counterexamples to Baum–Connes and Kadison–Kaplansky
title.subtitle: Claim: a torsion-free group with a projection of trace strictly between 0 and $1/2$ in its reduced C*-algebra

beats.text: Kadison–Kaplansky: for torsion-free $G$, the only projections are 0 and 1

Another group carries an irrational trace, which assembly cannot reach (Lück)

plain: Two big conjectures said some symmetry algebras hold no 'fractional' pieces; here are groups where they do

steps: Build a group from labelled expander-like graphs
A matrix over the group then has a gap in its spectrum
Cut at the gap: a projection with a forbidden trace

voice.text: For torsion-free groups, the only projections were supposed to be zero and one.
Build groups from expander graphs; cutting at a spectral gap yields a projection.
Claimed: a projection with trace below one half.
